gate_max_detector.topology: diode-OR of ten 1k branches into a 22k/6.2k divider
gate_max_detector.lm393_common_mode_source: references/datasheets/lm393.txt (SLCS005AH, revised April 2025; section 5.8, VICR row)

clamp.reason: a Zener knee is specified at a test current; this node spends tens of microamps, where the knee voltage is not bounded

unqualified_prerequisites: per-gate worst-case VGS at the fault temperature and device spread: the detector reports that a gate is above ~1 V, not that the FET is off; the engineer-reviewed safe-off threshold still has to be written down
detector diode drop over -40..+125 C and its spread (no vendored datasheet), which moves the trip between the ideal 0.942 V and VGS(th) min 1.3 V

the LM393's common-mode limit is now a cited number (§5.8: 3.5 V at 25 C, 3.0 V over the full range), but the 15 V standoff puts the all-ten sense node 0.29 V above the full-range row; it is permitted because the 0.200 V reference on the other input is in range, and that reading needs bench confirmation at the temperature extremes rather than at 25 C
ten-step bring-up sweep plus all-three-rails startup/collapse records; a sum or a maximum cannot show which channel is open

the response budget is a floor, not a worst case: tools/d0_response_budget.py now settles the permit rail, both driver datasheets' disable delays, the LM393 typical response, the CD4013 set-to-output max and the external fast path's CD4069UB/CD4071B pair (25 C maxima only), but the LM393 publishes no maximum at all, the UCC27524A's own switching numbers are not production-tested, and the 48/50-V 120-A fault cases are not swept
TL431 reference stability with C7 and min/max shunt current
power-on reset/ACK debounce and rail sequencing on actual hardware
real connected VGS probe records for all ten gates; ERC is not that evidence
